newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Kim's speech little initial impact on Seoul shares.
newsitem.headline: Kim's speech little initial impact on Seoul shares.

text.p: President Kim Young-sam's address to the South Korean nation on Tuesday morning had little immediate impact on the bourse, brokers said.
The shares rose 2.65 points to 679.24 about 20 minutes into trading, after Kim apologised for the Hanbo Steel loan scandal.
"We'll have to wait until the speech has been fully digested by investors, but we don't think that it will have any major impact," said Cha Hee-gun, a market analyst with Sunkyong Securities.
During his speech, Kim pledged to speed financial reform to eliminate corruption in the financial sector.
Brokers said local newspaper reports that the foreign shareholdings ceiling would be raised to 23 percent from the current 20 percent in April had a bigger effect on the market.
The finance ministry denied reports the limit would be eased twice in 1997, once in the first half and again in the second.
Chip makers rose after Merrill Lynch recommended U.S. memory chip stocks Micron Technology and Texas Instruments as unit demand for PCs remained strong.
Samsung Electronics rose 700 won to 54,500, Hyundai Electronics gained 400 won to 32,000, and LG Semicon climbed 100 won to 23,900.
